title: Corrected exceptional-set dimension bounds for random S-adic cocycles on Oseledets subspaces containing the unstable bundle
source_title: Hölder regularity for the spectrum of translation flows; Corrigendum to “Hölder regularity for the spectrum of translation flows”
author: Alexander I. Bufetov; Boris Solomyak
difficulty_reason: Oseledets estimates and the cited exponential-tail result do not directly bound the exceptional set of parameters uniformly over the frequency interval. The author builds a lattice-prediction scheme, counts its exceptional choices by an entropy estimate, and combines the unstable-projection cover with the complementary Oseledets directions. The corrected order of choosing the parameters is essential to that dimension bound, and the entire authored covering construction remains in the packet.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Only independent Proposition5.4 with official212 corrected quantifier order; not the translation-flow spectral bound. Full vector lattice-prediction, entropy covering and unstable projection argument retained. Theorem4.1 hypotheses—including integer substitution cocycle, integrability, positive Lyapunov exponents and the stated conditional exponential moment—are preserved. Existing exponential-tail Proposition4.2 is explicitly cited research foundation. No finite Hausdorff measure at the exact critical covering exponent is claimed; only the stated Hausdorff dimension bound. No uniform positive rho independent of epsilon1 as the superseded statement had. Official corrigendum212 read completely: corrected statement on combined35 supersedes old quantifiers on25 and explicitly says the original proposition proof needs no changes. Both original versions remain visible and separately hash-bound. Quantitative rho is chosen after epsilon1, before typical a and smaller delta. Standard covering bound gives Hausdorff dimension via an arbitrarily larger Hausdorff exponent; the intermediate claim of finite measure at its exact exponential-cover exponent is not selected. No independent numerical repair or reproof.
